unit_title: Unit 4: Indigenous Knowledge - Vocabulary,Reported Speech Focus
content: Unit 4: Vocabulary Focus - Indigenous Knowledge & Reported Speech (Communicative English Skills II - EnLa102) ========================================= 1. CORE CONCEPTS AND VOCABULARY OF INDIGENOUS KNOWLEDGE ========================================= What is Indigenous Knowledge (IK)? Indigenous Knowledge (IK) refers to the unique, traditional, local knowledge existing within and developed around the specific conditions of women and men indigenous to a particular geographic area (የሀገር በቀል እውቀት ማለት በአንድ አካባቢ በሚኖሩ የህብረተሰብ ክፍሎች ለትውልድ ሲወራረድ የመጣ የአካባቢን ችግር የመፍቻ እውቀት ነው)። Key Textual Vocabulary & Antonyms (Activity 4.6): 1. Persuasive (አሳማኝ/አማኝ) ↔ Unconvincing (ማያምን / አጠራጣሪ) - Example: The passage presents persuasive arguments for integrating indigenous knowledge into modern development. 2. Solidarity (አንድነት / መተባበር) ↔ Discord (መለያየት / አለመግባባት) - Example: Indigenous practices foster social solidarity among community members. 3. Open / Unrestricted (ክፍት / ያልተገደበ) ↔ Restricted (የተገደበ) - Example: Traditional knowledge sharing was often open to all community members. 4. Reduce (ቀነሰ / ማነስ) ↔ Increase (ጨመረ / ማደግ) - Example: Local healthcare knowledge has helped reduce child mortality in many regions. 5. Orthodox (መደበኛ / ተቀባይነት ያለው) ↔ Peculiar (ልዩ / ያልተለመደ) - Example: Orthodox science is beginning to acknowledge the value of local ecological practices. ========================================= 2. COMPREHENSIVE GRAMMAR MATRIX: DIRECT & INDIRECT (REPORTED) SPEECH ========================================= A. Tense Backshifting Rules (የጊዜ ግስ ለውጥ ህጎች) When the main reporting verb is in the past tense (e.g., said, told, asked, inquired), the verb tense in the reported clause steps one tense back into the past: - Present Simple → Past Simple: - Direct: "I love Ireland," Tedla said. - Indirect: Tedla said that he loved Ireland. - Present Continuous → Past Continuous: - Direct: "What are you doing here?" Betru asked. - Indirect: Betru asked him what he was doing there. - Present Perfect → Past Perfect: - Direct: "I have just come back from Nekemte," Tedla said. - Indirect: Tedla mentioned that he had just come back from Nekemte. - Past Simple → Past Perfect: - Direct: "Did you enjoy it?" Betru asked. - Indirect: Betru asked if he had enjoyed it. - Modals (Will/Can/May → Would/Could/Might): - Direct: "I can show you some pictures," Tedla offered. - Indirect: Tedla said that he could show him some pictures. B. Pronoun & Time/Place Adverb Transformations - Pronouns: Shift according to speaker and context (I → he/she, we → they, my → his/her). - Adverbs of Time & Place: - Now → Then - Today → That day - Tomorrow → The next day / the following day - Yesterday → The day before / the previous day - Here → There - This/These → That/Those C. Reporting Questions (Wh- Questions vs Yes/No Questions) - Wh- Questions: Retain the question word (what, where, why, how), but change question word-order into statement word-order (Subject + Verb). - Direct: "Where did you live?" they asked. - Indirect: They wanted to know where I had lived. - Yes/No Questions: Introduce with if or whether, followed by statement word-order. - Direct: "Is Prague the capital?" we asked. - Indirect: We needed to know whether Prague was the capital. ========================================= 3. ADVANCED GRAMMAR RULES, EXAM PITFALLS & SPECIAL CASES ========================================= Rule 1: Present Reporting Verbs (No Tense Shift) When the reporting verb is in the Present Tense (says, tells, asks), the tense inside the reported clause does NOT change. ❌ Incorrect: Dad says that he had lost his voice. ✅ Correct: Dad says that he has lost his voice. Rule 2: Universal Facts & Permanent Truths Statements expressing absolute scientific truths or general facts do not require tense backshifting when reported. - Direct: "Honey is good for your throat," Mum said. - Indirect: Mum explained that honey is good for the throat. Rule 3: Difference Between 'Say' and 'Tell' - Tell must be directly followed by a personal object (e.g., told me, told Tedla). - Say is NOT followed by a personal object unless 'to' is used (e.g., said that..., said to me). ❌ Incorrect: Betru told that he was free tonight. ✅ Correct: Betru said that he was free tonight. Rule 4: Reporting Imperatives and Commands Commands and requests use [Reporting Verb] + Object + to / not to + Base Verb (V1). - Direct: "Try moving it," Rahel said. - Indirect: Rahel told her to try moving it. ========================================= 4. PRACTICE EXAM QUESTIONS WITH DETAILED EXPLANATIONS ========================================= Question 1: What is the antonym of the word "discord" as used in the passage on indigenous knowledge? A. Conflict B. Solidarity C. Friction D. Isolation Correct Answer: B. Solidarity Explanation: 'Discord' means disagreement or conflict, whereas 'solidarity' means unity and agreement among community members. Question 2: Tedla: "I have just come back from my holiday in Nekemte." Which is the correct reported speech? A. Tedla said that he has just come back from his holiday in Nekemte. B. Tedla said that he had just come back from his holiday in Nekemte. C. Tedla says that he had just come back from his holiday in Nekemte. D. Tedla told he had just come back from his holiday in Nekemte. Correct Answer: B. Tedla said that he had just come back from his holiday in Nekemte. Explanation: Present perfect ('have come') changes to past perfect ('had come') when reported with a past reporting verb ('said'). Question 3: "Where did you live?" - They wanted to know ________. A. where did I live B. where I had lived C. where I live D. whether I lived Correct Answer: B. where I had lived Explanation: In reported Wh- questions, the auxiliary 'did' is dropped, word order becomes statement order (Subject + Verb), and past simple changes to past perfect. Question 4: Mark: "Dad says that he ________ his voice." A. lost B. had lost C. has lost D. losing Correct Answer: C. has lost Explanation: Because the reporting verb 'says' is in the present tense, the tense inside the reported clause remains in the present perfect ('has lost'). Question 5: Which word in the passage is opposite in meaning to "unconvincing"? A. Anecdotal B. Orthodox C. Persuasive D. Peculiar Correct Answer: C. Persuasive Explanation: 'Unconvincing' means not credible/convincing, making 'persuasive' its exact opposite.
